# Project

## project/instrukt/concept/purpose

- instrukt = modular Rust CLI for context engineering: documentation instructs agents through progressive retrieval and publication.
- why = a model knows how to code, not what is true on a machine, in a codebase and a business; instrukt keeps that in git, reviewed like code, and gives each task the exact piece it needs when it needs it.

## project/instrukt/policy/shared-workflows

- this project's shared workflows repository = `InstruktAI/workflows`, the InstruktAI organisation's own: the within-organisation case of `sdlc/policy/ci-pipeline-conventions`.
- MUST compose from it at a released version and route improvements and divergences through it -- it is the project's own code, not a stranger's.
- MUST, as reviewer, apply that policy's enforcement with `InstruktAI/workflows` as the existing path for generic pipeline logic.

# General

## general/principle/trust-and-guardrails

- MUST trust agents; gate only harm restoring state cannot repair: interference (two agents, one object) | contract changed under executor -- rest is brief's direction.
- NEVER meet irreversible mutation with permission rule; repair state layer (versioning, soft removal) -- gate makes it permanent.
- MUST read object (holder, phase), NEVER caller rank -- rank drifts.
- MUST name refusal's door (sanctioned path keeping invariant); on refusal stop, tell someone -- door is path, not decision.
- focus = brief's operation set, cheap; integrity = interference/contract, on object, no human bypass; involvement record = audit only.
- NEVER block live human direction via eligible authoring session with agent conflict rules -- process authority governs.
- MUST widen object model when invariant inexpressible, NEVER add call site -- missing dimension.

# Sdlc

## sdlc/policy/state-storage

- MUST state, before durable state gets a home, its nature (authoritative | derived from a named source | external bookkeeping: fingerprints, cursors, delivery marks | transient), its one writing owner and its loss cost (nothing | recomputation | network transfer | repeated external effect | lost intent) -- the home follows from them.
- MUST have the owner persist state whose loss forces more than cheap local recomputation when learned, surviving restarts, installs and crashes; process memory holds only what start rebuilds without network or repeated effects, never the only copy -- restarts otherwise cost traffic and duplicated actions.
- MUST record the intent of an external effect durably before it when its outcome must be recognised -- recovery then completes or recognises it instead of repeating.
- MUST state how a derived store is rebuilt and the cost, network included; NEVER keep state of another nature inside it -- rebuilding destroys it.
- state file = small, bounded, one writer, read whole or by key, never queried across; one document per owner and scope, written whole and atomically (beside the previous, renamed over).
- database = grows without fixed bound, frequent partial updates, several writing processes, queries/indexes, or several records changed in one transaction.
- write-isolation unit = scope in which writers wait on each other (SQLite: one database file).
- MUST share a write-isolation unit only within one owning domain with a compatible write pattern; NEVER let background writers (pollers, outboxes, delivery queues, maintenance) share one with a path a person or agent waits on; a domain whose write pattern or lifecycle differs gets its own -- fewer files is no reason; shared waits add latency.
- MUST name each state's scope (machine | project | home | cluster); state of a responsibility moving between computers moves with it by a defined transfer -- else the new owner rebuilds it.
- MUST give a growing store its bound and retirement, keeping current state apart from history, logs and outboxes -- retention prunes history, never current state.
- applies to durable state a delivery introduces, relocates or changes; an existing store is brought in line when the change path touches it or by work for that purpose.
- enforcement = architecture records each piece of durable state and its review verifies it; work without reviewed architecture records it in the plan; build and commit review reject undeclared state or storage breaking these rules.
- MAY, for a tool with no background process whose every write runs in a bounded invocation (a command, or a scheduled run that exits) under one per-computer writer lock, share one database across its domains; the architecture names the lock as the unit and the invocations that hold it -- the lock already serializes all writers.

# Project

## project/instrukt/policy/checks-and-guards

- MUST check a prerequisite (configuration, credential, published procedure, installed service) where it enters: when written, at install, when the runner starts or takes a change; NEVER handle a missing one while running -- what runs uses only what entry admitted.
- gate = such an entry check refusing with its door; proof of ownership, a version gate on rebuildable state, or refusing instrukt's own files is no gate.
- instrukt's own places = the files, service units, crontab line, private Redis config and marked hook sections it generates, each named with its home when that is not `~/.instrukt`.
- MUST write own places whole on converge, consulting no record of earlier writes; NEVER remove anything because it is remembered as written -- a check on a place only instrukt writes protects nothing.
- MUST make a part depending on an outside service (runtime, Slack, Redis, network, model provider) retry until it returns and report its state to the operator, except best-effort unavailable notices (`project/instrukt/spec/feature/company/conversations`) and dead-letter announcements (`project/instrukt/spec/feature/runner/event-consumers`); any other failure of a part is a code defect -- outages pass, defects do not.
- MAY tell a person writing to a company's agent about their request and their own world (their service unreachable, the assistant unavailable a while); NEVER about instrukt internals; what instrukt cannot resolve goes to the operator -- a person acts only on their own world.
- MUST give each object generation a fixed native start key and thread ID that retries replay -- retries stay one generation.
- MUST start a new generation automatically for outstanding work after confirmed native archive or deletion, or after an idle thread is confirmed in a runtime project other than its checkout's own; NEVER touch a misplaced thread while it is busy -- wait until idle.
- native lifecycle owns provider detachment; neither a create receipt nor a misplacement rollover guarantees a physical-process exit.
- NEVER discard a record of older or unknown shape unless its spec names the source that rebuilds it; MUST migrate, never discard or expire, a person's stated choices and restrictions and records of external effects -- discarding is safe only when the rebuild source survives.
- applies to instrukt's product behaviour (runner, installation, hooks, company messaging, command preconditions), not the todo workflow's own rules; spec and code review enforce it on mechanisms a change adds or touches.
